newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD again shrugs off offer on tax talks.
newsitem.headline: German SPD again shrugs off offer on tax talks.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats on Monday shrugged off an offer from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling Christian Democrat-Free Democrat coaltion to hold new talks to push through an ambitious tax reform plan.

Peter Struck, parliamentary business manager for the Social Democrats (SPD) told German newspaper Express that the two sides could continue to square off in the upper house of parliament, where the issue is already under discussion, rejecting the coalition's renewed offer to find a compromise.

"Discussions about the widening of the tax base and coalition's reaction to the SPD's proposal can be discussed next week in the appropriate subcommittee in the upper house where talks have already begun," Struck told the newspaper.
The Kohl government had hoped to push through an ambitious tax reform plan in time to fire up economic growth which could help secure Germany's entry into currency union.
But since no compromise was reached the proposal was moved to the upper house where the SPD, holding a majority, could block the plans.
